# Verify

> Verify (@revyl/verify) is an open-source TypeScript library for Revyl. It opens cloud browsers and iOS/Android devices for agent instruction/validation steps, or Mac computers for commands, files, processes, screenshots, and optional private recording metadata after release. Call it from a plain script, coding agent, CI, or any test runner. It has no test runner of its own.

## Docs

Mac computers are early access; ask support@revyl.ai about access. See computers.md#availability-and-errors.

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): install, authenticate, init, run a script
- [API](api.md): open(), attach(), hosted children, navigate(), report(), agent steps, screenshot(), exec(), file/process methods, close()
- [Configuration](configuration.md): verify.config.ts targets, environment variables, the init and whoami commands
- [Web](web.md): Revyl web sessions, URLs and builds, sign-in, steps, and exact actions
- [Mobile](mobile.md): iOS and Android devices, installing apps, and exact actions
- [Computers](computers.md#availability-and-errors): Mac early access, expiry, capacity errors, recording metadata, and confirmed release
- [Verify working end to end](end-to-end.md): live verification scope, observed outcomes, and limits of the evidence
- [CI and test runners](ci.md): GitHub Actions, node:test, Vitest, Jest, Playwright Test
- [Use your own model](own-model.md): run instructions and validations on Claude, GPT, Gemini, a local model or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; providers, limits, privacy and troubleshooting
- [Errors](errors.md): every error code and what to do about it
- [For coding agents](agents.md): the workflow and rules for agents using Verify, and the coordinate rule for exact actions

## Exact actions and coordinates

Prefer a description, such as `tap({ target: 'Sign in button' })`: Revyl finds the element on the current screen, and you never handle coordinates. Otherwise a point is `{ x, y }` in screenshot pixels on every platform: whole numbers from the top-left corner of the image `screenshot()` returns. So a position you read off a screenshot goes to `tap()`, `type()` and `swipe()` unchanged. `screenSize()` returns the screenshot's width and height, and `locate()` and the points `tap()` and `type()` return use the same pixels. A point outside the screenshot is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before any action is sent, and the message names the valid range. On iOS, Verify converts the pixels to the screen's points for you. On Web they equal CSS pixels at the default device scale factor of 1, and you still pass screenshot pixels at any other. This holds from TypeScript 0.4.1, Python 0.2.1 and Go v0.3.1; earlier versions took iOS points. See [For coding agents](agents.md#exact-actions-and-coordinates) for a runnable example.
